href="#clock-synchronization-and-multi-node-alignment">Clock Synchronization And Multi-Node Alignment</a> <a href="#controller-co-residency-controller-as-dut">Controller Co-Residency (Controller-As-DUT)</a> <a href="#repetition-ordering-and-thermal-equilibrium">Repetition, Ordering, And Thermal Equilibrium</a> <a href="#statistical-protocol">Statistical Protocol</a></aside> <div class="doc-wrap doc-source-docs-contracts-measurement-methodology-md"> <p class="doc-meta"><a href="library.html">Back to sources</a> · rendered from <code>docs/contracts/measurement_methodology.md</code></p> <div class="provenance-plate"><span class="source-chip" title="docs/contracts/measurement_methodology.md · commit 6d80039"><span class="source-file">docs/<wbr>contracts/<wbr>measurement_methodology.md</span><span class="source-commit">commit 6d80039</span></span></div> <!-- rendered: marked@18.0.6 --> <h1>Measurement Methodology</h1> <p>Living cross-phase contract, drafted in Phase 1. Changes require a decision-log entry when they bind later work.</p> <h2 id="measurement-principle">Measurement Principle</h2> <p>Every benchmark run must be reproducible from its raw artifacts. Summary metrics are derived outputs, not the source of truth.</p> <p>The source of truth for a run is the run bundle:</p> <ul> <li>Experiment config.</li> <li>Device and environment metadata.</li> <li>Event log with phase timestamps.</li> <li>Raw power trace.</li> <li>Raw model output.</li> <li>Reducer output.</li> <li>Runtime and telemetry logs.</li> </ul> <h2 id="run-lifecycle">Run Lifecycle</h2> <p>Before a campaign creates a run bundle, the operator runs the read-only doctor preflight described in <code>docs/contracts/doctor_preflight.md</code>. Schema-0.1 parsing continues to warn-and-ignore unknown keys for compatibility, but campaign execution fails before the first bundle when those warnings have not been explicitly acknowledged. The terminal campaign-verdict JSONL row records the exact warning set and acknowledgement; acknowledgement does not alter config bytes, collection evidence, claim readiness, or claim outcomes.</p> <p>Doctor also exposes architecture/version, configured model and tokenizer identity, requested sampler fields, inspect-only powermetrics privilege policy, thermal pressure, backup capacity, and quiet-machine warnings. These are preflight observations, not substitutes for per-bundle provenance or live measurement gates. In particular, doctor never starts powermetrics and never certifies that a machine is quiet.</p> <h3>Environment guard and per-run admission (D-077)</h3> <p>Campaigns select a strictly typed policy sidecar. <code>run_campaign.py</code> defaults to <code>configs/campaign_policies/quiet_mac_p2_production.json</code>, records the policy version and exact source-byte SHA-256 in campaign provenance and every member bundle, acquires the campaign lock, and only then performs the enforcing environment preflight before member 1. The production quiet-Mac guard requires AC power and an externally connected power source, low-power mode off, all online displays asleep, the screensaver disengaged, and Nominal thermal pressure. Unknown critical probes fail closed. Load averages are recorded as preflight evidence only and never gate a member.</p> <p>Default operation is verify-only. <code>--arm-quiet-mode</code> is an explicit transient operation: the runner displays a countdown, requests <code>pmset displaysleepnow</code>, and repeats the complete environment probe before deciding admission. It does not write display-sleep, screensaver, or other persistent host settings. An operator override is accepted only when its JSON binds the exact failed snapshot and findings SHA-256 values and records a reason, approver, and timestamp. It is stored as an <code>override</code>, not a waiver, and universally bars all resulting members from gross-energy, idle-subtracted-energy, and throughput claims.</p> <p>At each governed member&#39;s idle-baseline stage, the controller captures the same critical environment evidence and verifies that the display remains asleep and the screensaver remains disengaged. Awake, engaged, or unknown state aborts immediately. The first idle baseline is admitted only when the existing powermetrics GPU-idle-quality classification records <code>idle_window_suspect == false</code>. One and only one complete retry is allowed; both attempts preserve distinct raw artifacts and provenance. A persistent failure either aborts (production) or records the exploratory-only, unwaivable <code>environment_admission_failed</code> claim barrier (<code>on_fail: flag</code>). There is no skip disposition in a fixed-n campaign. A lightweight post-run display/screensaver/HID observation makes within-member transitions visible.</p> <p>The sidecar is deliberately separate from <code>BenchmarkConfig</code>. Direct <code>joulewise run</code> without a sidecar retains legacy flag-only/non-enforcing behavior, and omission of the additive policy/admission metadata preserves legacy normalized config serialization and hashes.</p> <h3>Per-bundle source provenance</h3> <p><code>RunBundleWriter.create</code> captures the harness source state before it creates bundle artifacts or returns control to any adapter. <code>write_metadata</code> captures the end state after adapter execution. <code>metadata.git_commit</code> remains the creation-time commit for compatibility; the governed record is <code>metadata.source_provenance</code> with schema <code>joulewise.source_provenance.v1</code>.</p> <p>Each <code>start</code> and <code>end</code> snapshot records <code>git_commit</code>, <code>tracked</code>, <code>staged</code>, <code>untracked</code>, and <code>diff_sha256</code>. The three state values are independently:</p> <ul> <li><code>clean</code>: the corresponding Git probe succeeded and found no change;</li> <li><code>dirty</code>: an unstaged tracked diff, staged diff, or non-ignored untracked path was present, respectively; or</li> <li><code>unknown</code>: the corresponding probe or required file read failed. Failure is never interpreted as clean.</li> </ul> <p>The privacy-safe diff identity descriptor is <code>sha256</code> / <code>joulewise.git-diff.nul-v1</code>. The producer captures the byte output of <code>git diff --no-ext-diff --no-textconv --binary</code>, the analogous <code>--cached</code> command, and <code>git ls-files --others --exclude-standard -z</code>. For each sorted untracked path it hashes, without serializing, the NUL-safe length-framed path, file kind, mode, size, and SHA-256 of regular-file bytes or symlink-target bytes. The final identity is SHA-256 over the version plus length-framed <code>tracked</code>, <code>staged</code>, and untracked-inventory byte identities. Bundles contain only the final digest and state labels: never a diff, path, untracked file content, or secret.</p> <p><code>changed_during_run</code> is true when two fully known snapshots differ, false when they match, and null when either snapshot is not fully known. <code>claim_eligible</code> is true only when both commits and diff identities are known, all six component states are clean, and the snapshots match. <code>reason_codes</code> is the deterministic list of every start/end unknown or dirty component followed, when applicable, by <code>source_changed_during_run</code>. Bundle completion remains allowed in every state so raw evidence is not discarded.</p> <p>Dirty, unknown, changed, missing, or internally inconsistent provenance is a hard exclusion for claim-bearing use. The publication pack preflight enforces that boundary and refuses such bundles. Analysis-side admission propagation is separate from capture and field semantics and is owned by WO-004/T11.</p> <ol> <li>Validate config.</li> <li>Create run directory.</li> <li>Collect device metadata.</li> <li>Measure idle baseline.</li> <li>Warm up runtime.</li> <li>Wait the configured post-warmup settling interval (<code>sampling.warmup_seconds</code>; zero means no wait).</li> <li>Start measured telemetry.</li> <li>Run workload.</li> <li>Stop measured telemetry.</li> <li>Cleanup runtime.</li> <li>Reduce raw artifacts into summary metrics.</li> </ol> <p>The post-warmup settling interval begins only after all active <code>workload_profile.warmup_runs</code> calls and their clock-alignment captures have completed. It ends before the measured-run stage and sampling-active markers, so it is never integrated into the measured window. Controller events record the configured value on the warmup completion event and the runtime log records positive waits.</p> <h2 id="idle-subtraction">Idle Subtraction</h2> <p>Energy metrics must report both gross and idle-subtracted values when possible. The idle baseline is measured before each run and stored in the run bundle.</p> <p>Minimum idle fields:</p> <ul> <li><code>idle_power_w_mean</code></li> <li><code>idle_power_w_stddev</code></li> <li><code>idle_duration_s</code></li> <li><code>idle_sample_count</code></li> <li><code>telemetry_backend</code></li> </ul> <h2 id="thermal-state">Thermal State</h2> <p>Each telemetry backend should report thermal state before and after measured runs when the platform exposes it.</p> <p>Minimum thermal fields:</p> <ul> <li><code>temperature_c</code></li> <li><code>thermal_pressure</code> or platform equivalent, when available.</li> <li><code>fan_state</code> or cooling mode, when available.</li> </ul> <h2 id="uncertainty">Uncertainty</h2> <p>Phase 1 defines uncertainty fields; Phase 2 implements reducer behavior. Repeated runs should report:</p> <ul> <li>Number of repetitions.</li> <li>Mean.</li> <li>Standard deviation.</li> <li>Confidence interval method.</li> <li>Confidence interval bounds.</li> </ul> <h2 id="measurement-quality-fields">Measurement Quality Fields</h2> <p>Each run summary should include:</p> <ul> <li>Sampling rate requested.</li> <li>Sampling rate observed.</li> <li>Dropped or malformed samples.</li> <li>Idle variance.</li> <li>Thermal drift.</li> <li>Telemetry source.</li> <li>Local runtime cleanup result (<code>runtime_cleanup_ok</code>: true/false/null). Cleanup occurs after the measured window, so failure is a quality concern for the following repetition and does not retroactively change current-run status or energy.</li> <li>Wall-meter comparison delta, when available.</li> </ul> <h2 id="phase-labels">Phase Labels</h2> <p>The event log should use stable phase names:</p> <ul> <li><code>idle</code></li> <li><code>warmup</code></li> <li><code>prefill</code></li> <li><code>decode</code></li> <li><code>serialize</code></li> <li><code>transfer</code></li> <li><code>deserialize</code></li> <li><code>cleanup</code></li> <li><code>failure</code></li> </ul> <p><code>deserialize</code> (cache load on the decode node) was added 2026-06-09 alongside the split-run accounting definitions (see <code>docs/phase_3/phase_3_plan.md</code>); phase labels are strings in the schema, so the addition is non-breaking. Split-stage accounting, pinned so reducers and prose agree: serialize = cache-persist window on the prefill node; transfer = byte-movement window; deserialize = cache-load window on the decode node; decode = first-token to last-token. Cache load is not decode energy.</p> <h2 id="hardware-classification">Hardware Classification</h2> <p>Every target should end Phase 1 in one state:</p> <ul> <li><code>supported</code>: known viable and ready for Phase 2 implementation.</li> <li><code>pending</code>: expected viable but not fully checked.</li> <li><code>unsupported</code>: not viable for a documented technical reason.</li> </ul> <h2 id="measurement-boundaries">Measurement Boundaries</h2> <p>&quot;Power&quot; means a different physical boundary on each telemetry backend. Cross-target absolute comparisons must state the boundary difference; the final report&#39;s limitations section inherits this table. Decision D-018 defines the rail policy (per-rail trace rows plus a per-backend rail manifest naming the canonical sum).</p> <div class="table-scroll"><table> <thead> <tr> <th>Backend</th> <th>Boundary</th> <th>Included</th> <th>Excluded</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody><tr> <td>powermetrics</td> <td>Apple SoC subsystems</td> <td>CPU + GPU + ANE package power</td> <td>display, storage, memory at wall, PSU losses</td> </tr> <tr> <td>nvidia_smi</td> <td>GPU board</td> <td>board power as reported by driver</td> <td>host CPU, DRAM, motherboard, PSU losses</td> </tr> <tr> <td>jetson_rails</td> <td>module input (VDD_IN preferred; actual rail recorded)</td> <td>module power</td> <td>carrier-board peripherals (rail-dependent), PSU losses</td> </tr> <tr> <td>wall_meter</td> <td>full system AC</td> <td>everything incl. PSU losses</td> <td>nothing</td> </tr> <tr> <td>mock</td> <td>synthetic</td> <td>n/a</td> <td>n/a</td> </tr> </tbody></table></div> <p>Rules:</p> <ul> <li>Within-target comparisons (the same backend) are always boundary-consistent and are the primary claim type.</li> <li>Cross-target comparisons are reported with boundaries named; where the wall meter exists, the wall-vs-platform delta is recorded per target and used to contextualize the gap.</li> <li>Each telemetry adapter declares its rail manifest in <code>device_metadata</code>; the reducer sums exactly the manifest rails to produce <code>power_w</code>.</li> </ul> <h2 id="clock-synchronization-and-multi-node-alignment">Clock Synchronization And Multi-Node Alignment</h2> <p>Policy per decision D-003:</p> <ul> <li>Canonical <code>timestamp_s</code> everywhere is epoch UTC from <code>time.time()</code> via the injected clock; no other time base appears in artifacts.</li> <li>Each process records its monotonic-vs-wall offset at start in metadata (detects wall-clock steps mid-run).</li> <li>Each node records NTP sync state in metadata when determinable.</li> <li>For multi-node runs, the controller bounds per-node clock offset with marker events: timestamp a no-op command on the remote node immediately before and after each remote stage; half the round trip bounds the offset. The bound is recorded in composite-bundle metadata.</li> <li>Reducers must flag (in measurement quality) any cross-node interval shorter than the recorded offset bound; such intervals are not used for energy attribution claims.</li> <li>Required precision: at 1-10 Hz power sampling, tens of milliseconds - comfortably within LAN NTP plus the marker bound.</li> </ul> <h2 id="controller-co-residency-controller-as-dut">Controller Co-Residency (Controller-As-DUT)</h2> <p>On Mac-local runs the controller process runs on the measured machine. Mitigation per decision D-013:</p> <ul> <li>The idle baseline is measured with the controller resident and quiescent, so the controller&#39;s floor load is included in what idle subtraction removes.</li> <li>During the measured window the controller only blocks on the runtime: no logging, no polling, no file writes; log records buffer in memory and flush after sampling stops.</li> <li>Residual risk is recorded, not hidden: OS background activity affects idle and measured windows alike; the upgrade path (remote-controlled Mac runs once the SSH transport exists) is queued as a validation comparison.</li> </ul> <h2 id="repetition-ordering-and-thermal-equilibrium">Repetition, Ordering, And Thermal Equilibrium</h2> <p>Per decisions D-005 and D-014:</p> <ul> <li>Each repetition is an independent run bundle; an experiment manifest groups members and records the executed order.</li> <li>Between live repetitions, cooldown v2 holds until the retained evidence has both a complete 30-second wall-clock span and at least <code>coverage_fraction * sustained_window_s</code> of captured coverage (<code>coverage_fraction = 0.8</code> by default), and its duration-weighted idle-power mean satisfies the one-sided rule <code>rolling_mean &lt;= reference * (1 + tolerance)</code> (10% by the production policy), while thermal pressure is Nominal. A below-reference mean therefore counts as recovery. An optional calibrated absolute ceiling is an additional upper cap and never an OR escape. The wait has a 5-minute cap; the cap is evaluated before release on every iteration, so recovery criteria first met at or after the deadline remain a <code>cap_hit</code> (with the late criteria recorded in the trace) and are recorded in the following repetition&#39;s measurement quality.</li> <li>The preceding baseline is eligible as a cooldown reference only when <code>idle_window_suspect == false</code>, all critical environment probes passed, and policy/environment provenance is present. An ineligible or unknown reference falls back to one frozen clean anchor: the NEG-8 reference start when present, otherwise the first admission-passing baseline. The anchor&#39;s source and hashes are recorded and it is never updated from later outcomes. With neither an eligible reference nor an anchor the gate fails closed. The following member records policy version, eligibility decision, anchor provenance, thresholds (including <code>coverage_fraction</code>), wall-clock span, required and observed coverage, thermal result, and the exact release criterion under <code>preceding_campaign_cooldown</code>. Historical recovered rows retain their recorded meaning and are not reinterpreted.</li> <li>Conditions are interleaved round-robin where model-reload cost permits; where blocks are operationally forced, the order is recorded so drift correlation can be audited (Phase 4 Stage 4.5 does this audit).</li> </ul> <h2 id="statistical-protocol">Statistical Protocol</h2> <p>Per decision D-014 (draft to be ratified against observed variance at Phase 4 Stage 4.0), amended 2026-07-09 (C-023 S3; amendments ratified by D-053):</p> <ul> <li>Repetitions: n &gt;= 5 for headline comparisons; n &gt;= 3 minimum elsewhere; the n is recorded per experiment.</li> <li>Intervals: report mean, sample standard deviation, and 95% confidence interval via Student t; Phase 4 runs a bootstrap sensitivity comparison and reports both where they materially disagree.</li> <li>Outliers: flagged by modified z-score on MAD &gt; 3.5; never silently dropped; reported with-and-without only when a physical cause is identified and documented; otherwise kept in headline numbers. Amendment 2026-07-09 (C-023 S3, ratified by D-053): at n &lt;= 10, reports also run a leave-one-out influence check on every claim-bearing contrast. The report lists the full-data estimate/CI/verdict and each leave-one-out estimate/CI/verdict. An omitted point is influential if it changes the sign, floor status, adjusted rejection/equivalence verdict, or moves the estimate by more than 0.25 x the active threshold: MDE for rank/MDE-gated claims, otherwise the floor gate. Influential points are reported as sensitivity evidence, not silently removed.</li> <li>Figures always show raw points alongside aggregates.</li> <li>Amendment 2026-07-09 (C-023 S3, ratified by D-053): differences are claimed from the confidence interval of the paired/block difference, or from the named model contrast, not by visual separation of marginal intervals. Where execution order was randomized, the analysis includes a permutation/randomization check for the same contrast following the actual randomization scheme, permuting labels only within exchangeable blocks/strata. The minimum for this check is 6 exchangeable blocks; below that count, report the check as not run and rely on the contrast CI with the caveat that randomization-inference sensitivity was underpowered. A paired contrast is preferred when it matches the design; mixed or hierarchical models are reserved for real dependence structures that a paired/block contrast cannot represent. Floor-gated outcomes use a three-way rule: below-floor contrasts are <code>not resolvable</code>; above-floor contrasts whose CI does not support direction are <code>unresolved</code> with no directional claim; equivalence or &quot;no difference&quot; language requires a predeclared equivalence gate whose margin exceeds the floor and whose contrast CI lies entirely within that margin.</li> </ul> </div> </div> </main> <footer class="site"> <div class="inner"> <span>JouleWise · github.com/mpmdw/JouleWise</span> <span>docs/contracts/measurement_methodology.md · commit 6d80039 · regenerate: <span class="mono">python3 scripts/build_site.py</span></span> </div> </footer> </body> </html>

<a href="decision_log.html">Recent</a> · <strong aria-current="page">Archive 1</strong></nav> <div class="provenance-plate"><span class="source-chip" title="docs/decision_log.md · commit 1af9f92 + uncommitted"><span class="source-file">docs/<wbr>decision_log.md</span><span class="source-commit">commit 1af9f92 + uncommitted</span></span></div> <!-- rendered: marked@18.0.6 --> <h1>Decision Log</h1> <p>This is the canonical record of design decisions for JouleWise. Every decision that binds later work, trades off real alternatives, or would otherwise need to be re-derived by a future agent gets an entry here.</p> <h2 id="how-to-use-this-log">How To Use This Log</h2> <ul> <li>Before implementing anything non-trivial, check whether a decision here already covers it. Do not silently re-decide settled questions.</li> <li>When you make a new decision of this kind during a run, add an entry, link it from the run report, and reference its ID (<code>D-NNN</code>) in the code review or doc that applies it.</li> <li>Statuses: <code>accepted</code> (binding until revisited), <code>open</code> (criteria defined, evidence pending), <code>proposed</code> (recorded, awaiting Ed&#39;s ratification), <code>superseded by D-NNN</code>.</li> <li>Every entry must include Options Considered and Considerations. A decision without recorded alternatives is not auditable.</li> <li>Revisit triggers are part of the contract: when a trigger fires, the decision must be re-examined, not quietly worked around.</li> </ul> <h2 id="index">Index</h2> <div class="table-scroll"><table> <thead> <tr> <th>ID</th> <th>Title</th> <th>Status</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody><tr> <td>D-001</td> <td>Run bundles store normalized <code>config.json</code>, not YAML</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-002</td> <td>Telemetry sampling via subprocess + file, no controller threading</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-003</td> <td>Timestamp and clock-alignment policy</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-004</td> <td><code>powermetrics</code> privilege workflow</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-005</td> <td>One bundle per repetition, grouped by experiment manifest</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-006</td> <td>Dashboard v1 is a static HTML report generator</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-007</td> <td>YAML config input is deferred</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-008</td> <td>Split runs arrive via schema v0.2 (<code>run_kind</code> + <code>split_plan</code>)</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-009</td> <td>Dependency policy: stdlib core, optional extras</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-010</td> <td>Run ID scheme</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-011</td> <td><code>summary_metrics.json</code> is the bundle completion marker</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-012</td> <td>Failure-reason to run-status mapping</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-013</td> <td>Controller-as-DUT mitigation for Mac-local runs</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-014</td> <td>Statistical protocol for repeated runs</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-015</td> <td>Split-mechanism priority and same-runtime rule</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-016</td> <td>Benchmark model selection</td> <td>open (provisional small-model pick 2026-07-06; opens 2G only)</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-017</td> <td>CI scope</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-018</td> <td>Per-backend <code>power_w</code> definition and rail policy</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-019</td> <td>Mock adapters use simulated time via an injectable clock</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-020</td> <td>CLI binds <code>FakeClock</code> for all-mock runs, <code>SystemClock</code> otherwise</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-021</td> <td>Controller flushes <code>events.jsonl</code> before the reduce stage</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-022</td> <td>Auto-generated run-ID suffix is config-hash-derived, not random</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-023</td> <td>Per-item phase status lives solely in the exit checklists</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-024</td> <td>Adapters receive a <code>RunContext</code>, not piecemeal parameters</td> <td>accepted; implemented (2N.1, 2026-07-06)</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-025</td> <td>One shared bundle read layer for reducer, report, validation, and aggregation</td> <td>accepted; implemented (2N.8, 2026-07-06)</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-026</td> <td>Measured window is bounded by sampling-active marker events</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-027</td> <td>Per-rail rows must share per-sample timestamps; misalignment is a structured failure</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-028</td> <td><code>reduce</code> verb rewrites <code>summary_metrics.json</code> in place (the one sanctioned post-finalize mutation)</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-029</td> <td>Config schema declares nullable optionals; serialization (and config hashes) unchanged</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-030</td> <td><code>validate-bundle</code> stays structural by default; <code>--strict</code> adds raw-evidence checks</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-031</td> <td>Multi-model council review; PR convention for multi-commit sessions (merge authority amended by C-010); D-023 extension + end-of-session consistency sweep</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-032</td> <td><code>phase_energy_j</code> is gross-only in summary v0.1</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-033</td> <td>Prompt-content provenance is recorded per run bundle</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-034</td> <td>Slice 2O owns the workload program after 2M and 3.0.1; implementation lane reopened by D-042</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-035</td> <td>Replay claims require fresh-process (subprocess-per-stage) isolation</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-036</td> <td>Spike verdict codes derive from measured data, never hardcoded</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-037</td> <td>Claims ladder (L0-L4) binds reader-facing claim language from 2M onward</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-038</td> <td>Analysis plans bind L2/L3 claims to pre-registered comparison rows</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-039</td> <td>Workload program v2: substrate first, identification before scale; pre-Window-A allowlist superseded by D-041/D-042</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-040</td> <td>Suite architecture v2: generic suite mechanism, bundle-level replication</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-041</td> <td>Benchmark interop via frozen-subset imports and marker-shim energy layer; interop lane remains post-2M + post-P2-010a</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-042</td> <td>D-034 implementation lane reopened; suite build may proceed pre-2M</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-043</td> <td>Supersession-closure discipline</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-044</td> <td>Suite config identity: omission-serialized ref + effective-manifest hash</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-045</td> <td>Suite substrate execution semantics (run_suite, statuses, per-item outputs)</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-046</td> <td>AP-6 sentinel delivery is ids-native BOS-less at literal equal shape</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-047</td> <td>Affine ladder pins: level set, smoke sizing, gate denominators</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-048</td> <td>Split program is model-first: pre-registered compositional prediction before split runs</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-049</td> <td>Split transfer-energy boundary accounting on discrete-GPU ends</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-050</td> <td>Active stop cards and process-trace manifests</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-051</td> <td>Advisor status site uses source-derived static pages plus fail-soft live GitHub overlays</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-052</td> <td>Capstone scope contract: frozen umbrella headline and contribution ladder</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-053</td> <td>Contrast-level statistical inference and the frozen analysis registry</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-054</td> <td>False-effect guard floor and unknown-term claim-ceiling policy</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-055</td> <td>Research-question registry is the canonical live index</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-056</td> <td>Suite order policies and order_row provenance</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-057</td> <td>Uncertainty terms: drift is a bound; stable claim-gate reason codes</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-058</td> <td>Token-normalization and stack-identity contract adopted</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-059</td> <td>Claims-lint mechanical enforcement in CI</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-060</td> <td>Depth-before-breadth stop line</td> <td>accepted (ratified 2026-07-10)</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-061</td> <td>Review-layer evaluation rule v2</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-062</td> <td>Confirmatory sampling policy (fixed n, demotion)</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-063</td> <td>Process architecture v2 (state kernel first)</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-064</td> <td>Delegated-invocation compliance surface: tracked per-session JSONL event stream, canonical report envelope, enforced write scope</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-065</td> <td>bridge-protocol/v1.1 — co-work lane, session wrappers, tolerant envelope</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-066</td> <td>Scoped spec-freeze override for the AXI extension agenda (Ed override)</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-067</td> <td>Idle reporting basis — gross headline; idle-subtracted is a labeled within-device secondary view</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-068</td> <td>Site deployment is Ed-manual; sessions end with a drift report, never a deploy</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-069</td> <td>Advisor-doc alignment (stream S-0) is sanctioned front-facing work</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-070</td> <td>Architectural-axes extension agenda (AXI): scope, claim posture, batch-axis rulings</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-071</td> <td>G10 memory-fit rule ratified (axi-sd-memory-fit-shape-v1); device-list review opened</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-072</td> <td>Standing self-merge-with-full-gate authority (gh merges included)</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td><a href="decision_log_archive_1.html#d-073">D-073</a></td> <td>D-016 device-list amendment: Mac + 3080 Ti primary fleet, 12 GiB cap</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td><a href="decision_log_archive_1.html#d-074">D-074</a></td> <td>Conditional Qwen3-4B primary repin + OLMo-1B conversion spike authorized</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td><a href="decision_log_archive_1.html#d-075">D-075</a></td> <td>Extension-axis intake: ranked fold-in without new thesis proliferation</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td><a href="decision_log_archive_1.html#d-076">D-076</a></td> <td>Site capacity right-sizing (AUD-WO-039 review): measured-first budgets</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td><a href="decision_log_archive_1.html#d-077">D-077</a></td> <td>Environment guard, idle admission, and cooldown v2</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td><a href="decision_log.html#d-078">D-078</a></td> <td>Soundness gate: no claim-bearing extraction from time-anchor-defective powermetrics corpora</td> <td>accepted; operative under Ed&#39;s direction through the full repair arc (close-out cap explicitly Ed-ratified 2026-07-22; original-text ratification rides PR #79 review)</td> </tr> </tbody></table></div> <hr> <blockquote> <p><strong>Site view:</strong> the complete entry index appears above; the 72 older full entries are omitted from this page for capsule size. The complete log is the repository file <a href="https://github.com/mpmdw/JouleWise/blob/main/docs/decision_log.md"><code>docs/decision_log.md</code></a>.</p> </blockquote> <span id="d-073"></span><h2 id="d-073-d-016-device-list-amendment-mac-3080-ti-primary-fleet-12-gib-cap">D-073: D-016 device-list amendment — Mac + 3080 Ti primary fleet, 12 GiB cap</h2> <p>Date: 2026-07-16. Owner: Ed (ruled on the D-071 brief, <code>docs/process_traces/2026-07-16-device-list-brief/brief.md</code>). The primary cross-target fleet is the 128 GB M3 Max Mac and the 3080 Ti (12 GiB) rig; the G10 capacity cap re-floors from 8 GiB to <strong>12 GiB</strong> (3080 Ti class sets the floor). Jetson hardware is retained as OPTIONAL, non-cap-setting replication — the edge/8 GiB cell can be added later as a replication row without re-deciding this. The split study&#39;s two nodes are the Mac and the 3080 Ti rig. Big models remain open via the Mac-only subsystem (D-071 clause 3). Follow-ons ruled by Ed same session: (a) conditional primary-model repin remains open with a WIDENED candidate search under the new cap (Ed: &quot;is there really nothing better than Qwen3-1.7B? Gemma 4B or something?&quot;) — 3-4B-class models now fit comfortably; (b) dense/MoE pair re-search under the 12 GiB cap (OLMo dense arm failed G4 as published — see the OLMo verification record in the same trace directory).</p> <span id="d-074"></span><h2 id="d-074-conditional-qwen3-4b-primary-repin-olmo-1b-conversion-spike-authorized">D-074: Conditional Qwen3-4B primary repin + OLMo-1B conversion spike authorized</h2> <p>Date: 2026-07-16. Owner: Ed (ruled on the 12 GiB model search, <code>docs/process_traces/2026-07-16-device-list-brief/model-search-12gib.md</code>). (1) Qwen3-4B becomes the D-016 primary CONDITIONALLY: the repin lands only when the evidence gates pass (immutable source/license, MLX-Q4/GGUF-Q4/CUDA artifact receipts, three-runtime generation, G10 at the 12 GiB cap, KV receipts, thinking-mode policy pinned); any gate failure retains Qwen2.5-1.5B. New evidence era on success: manifests + quant ladder regenerate from one frozen source revision; Qwen2.5 results preserved as legacy. Runner-up Qwen3-1.7B; Gemma-3-4B rejected for the gated custom license + multimodal MLX seam. (2) The time-boxed OLMo-1B original-format→MLX conversion spike is authorized; success revives the matched OLMoE pair, failure files the dated negative finding and the pair defers (Option C) without re-litigation. Both execute next session as agent-lane work.</p> <span id="d-075"></span><h2 id="d-075-extension-axis-intake-ranked-fold-in-without-new-thesis-proliferation">D-075: Extension-axis intake — ranked fold-in without new thesis proliferation</h2> <ul> <li>Date: 2026-07-17</li> <li>Status: accepted (Ed-directed intake via the 2026-07-17 evaluation)</li> <li>Phase: Phase 2+ research program</li> </ul> <p>Context: Ed directed a six-axis evaluation and ratified the resulting roadmap at <code>docs/process_traces/2026-07-17-extension-axes/roadmap-synthesis.md</code>. D-055 keeps C5 deliberation in the bank and the registry as the canonical live index; D-070 keeps these axes as stress tests of Q4, caps candidate commitments at L2, and reserves commitment authority to Ed. The disposition ledger is <code>docs/stream_logs/2026-07-17-axes-foldin.md</code>.</p> <p>Decision:</p> <ol> <li>Admit C5-2.5c as the primary speculative-decoding Q4 break-even rider, C5-2.5b as its proposal-work secondary, and C5-2.5d as a mandatory contamination control. Preserve C5-2.5a in the deliberative bank as a deferred candidate rider only; it is not a standalone campaign commitment before a prospective cross-mechanism design is affordable. All four retain the evaluation&#39;s exact ceilings and forbidden upgrades, and C-023-OUTPUT-IDENTITY is binding.</li> <li>Admit C5-2.11 as the on-device MLX quantized-KV candidate and attach it to C5-2.4, C5-1.12, and C-023-QUALITY-EQUIV-QUANT. Preserve C5-2.12, C5-2.13, and C5-2.14 only as candidate riders on the existing context/KV-growth, prompt-cache/replay, and Q4/AP-1 homes.</li> <li>Admit one new canonical RQ row, RQ-AXI-HYBRID-PAIR, at an L2 named-pair ceiling. Attach the attention/context-slope and module-attribution refinements to existing rows. Record kernel/backend provenance as amendments to C5-1.8, C5-2.7, and C5-3.3, not new theses.</li> <li>Keep the roadmap&#39;s do-not-fold set out of the canonical row set. Its negative dispositions and all unresolved feasibility questions remain in the stream ledger, including explicit <strong>NEEDS-WEB</strong> markers. Intake does not convert an unresolved runtime, model-pair, adapter, or device-fit question into a capstone commitment.</li> </ol> <p>Options considered:</p> <ol> <li>Mint every evaluated suggestion as an independent live question. Rejected: it duplicates existing homes, imports unidentifiable mechanism claims, and violates D-070&#39;s single-Q4-thesis posture.</li> <li>Admit only the top three ranked items. Rejected: the lower-cost controls, riders, and provenance amendments prevent predictable attribution errors without creating independent theses.</li> <li>Apply the roadmap&#39;s ranked fold-in and explicit exclusions. Chosen by Ed.</li> </ol> <p>Considerations: this is research-agenda intake, not campaign scheduling or evidence promotion. Every admitted candidate/rider remains floor-gated, earliest-phase tagged, capped at L2 unless an already-existing parent row&#39;s separate machinery says otherwise, and subject to its named forbidden upgrade. The published corpus remains claim-evidence-flagged; no fixture, runtime feasibility result, or registry entry is live energy evidence. D-070 remains the authority for Ed&#39;s axis commitments and quiet-Mac ordering.</p> <p>Revisit triggers: a relevant <strong>NEEDS-WEB</strong> feasibility finding lands; a named runtime/pair becomes unsupported; P2-015 floors make a predeclared effect undetectable; or Ed changes the D-070 commitment set. Revisit by amending the owning row and this decision&#39;s ledger, never by silently promoting an excluded candidate.</p> <span id="d-076"></span><h2 id="d-076-site-capacity-right-sizing-aud-wo-039-review-measured-first-budgets">D-076: Site capacity right-sizing (AUD-WO-039 review) — measured-first budgets</h2> <p>Date: 2026-07-17/18. Owner: lead under Ed&#39;s &quot;host the brief&quot; directive (the capacity decision event AUD-WO-039 fenced on). Ruling, encoded in tests with PR #76: the 1 MiB Lakebed hard cap is inviolate; the measured-artifact budget is 1,000,000 B (measured mode via the pinned validator, SITE-02 loud-discovery discipline); the 943,718 B conservative-estimate guard remains ONLY as fallback when measured mode is unavailable (estimator overshoot documented ~4.3% on identical input). WO-039 preservation boundary held: no advisor-facing page, navigation, provenance, or deep link trimmed. Current measured artifact 961,210 B. Revisit trigger: measured artifact within 24 KB of the hard cap forces the next right-sizing review before any addition.</p> <span id="d-077"></span><h2 id="d-077-environment-guard-idle-admission-and-cooldown-v2">D-077: Environment guard, idle admission, and cooldown v2</h2> <ul> <li>Date: 2026-07-17</li> <li>Status: accepted</li> <li>Phase: 2 / measurement</li> </ul> <p>Context: a Ventura video screensaver compositing on an awake display was identified as a material, repeatable contaminant. The affected windows showed about 50% GPU duty and were already detected by the existing <code>idle_window_suspect</code> thresholds. The campaign preflight, per-run admission, and D-014 cooldown nevertheless lacked one shared environment policy, exact override custody, and a sustained-window implementation. In particular, the old cooldown could release after one 5-second sub-window even though the contract called for a rolling 30-second recovery window.</p> <p>Options considered:</p> <ol> <li>Treat doctor output as a quietness certificate and continue to rely on operator judgment between members. Rejected: a point-in-time advisory cannot certify the later measured window and cannot enforce fixed-n admission.</li> <li>Change persistent display/screensaver preferences or allow contaminated members to be skipped or waived. Rejected: campaign preparation must not mutate host policy, and outcome-dependent skipping/waiving would break the fixed-n design and conceal the contamination.</li> <li>Use a hash-bound campaign-policy sidecar, an enforcing campaign preflight, per-run idle admission with one evidence-bearing retry, and cooldown v2 with frozen clean-anchor fallback. Chosen.</li> </ol> <p>Decision:</p> <ul> <li>A shared pure evaluator owns environment findings. Doctor consumes it only advisorily. <code>run_campaign.py</code> consumes it enforcingly after taking the campaign lock and before member 1. Critical unknowns fail closed. Load average is recorded as evidence but is never a member-admission gate.</li> <li>The production quiet-Mac policy requires AC power with an externally connected source, low-power mode off, all online displays asleep, the screensaver disengaged, and Nominal thermal pressure. Quiet-mode arming is explicit and transient: countdown, <code>pmset displaysleepnow</code>, then a complete re-probe. Persistent settings are never changed.</li> <li>An environment override must name the exact snapshot and findings digests it acknowledges. It is recorded as an override, never a waiver, and makes every resulting member universally claim-ineligible.</li> <li>Per-run idle admission reuses the validated <code>idle_window_suspect == false</code> threshold. It permits exactly one fully evidenced retry with distinct raw artifacts. Persistent awake-display, screensaver, or unknown critical state aborts immediately. Production aborts after retry; the exploratory-only <code>flag</code> path completes the fixed-n member but stamps the unwaivable <code>environment_admission_failed</code> reason on gross-energy, idle-subtracted-energy, and throughput claims. There is no skip action.</li> <li>Cooldown v2 amends D-014: recovery requires a complete, duration-weighted, sustained 30-second evidence window; the one-sided rule is <code>rolling_mean &lt;= reference * (1 + tolerance)</code>, so a below-reference window is recovered. Nominal thermal state is conjunctive. A calibrated absolute ceiling, when configured, is only an additional upper cap. A preceding baseline is reference-eligible only when its idle window is clean, critical environment checks passed, and policy/environment provenance is present. Otherwise the campaign uses one frozen clean anchor (NEG-8 reference start when present, else the first admission-passing baseline), records its provenance, never updates it from later outcomes, and fails closed when no eligible reference or anchor exists. Historical recovered rows are not reinterpreted.</li> <li>The policy owner is a strictly typed, byte-hashed sidecar under <code>configs/campaign_policies/</code>; policy version and SHA-256 are copied into each governed bundle. Campaign execution defaults to the production sidecar. Direct <code>joulewise run</code> without a sidecar retains legacy non-enforcing behavior. All bundle/config additions are nullable or omission-serialized; legacy normalized config bytes and hashes are unchanged.</li> <li>This amends D-057&#39;s stable claim-reason vocabulary by adding <code>environment_admission_failed</code> and <code>environment_override</code>. Both are universal and unwaivable for gross-energy, idle-subtracted-energy, and throughput claims.</li> </ul> <p>Considerations: environment admission is measurement-apparatus integrity, not post-hoc data cleaning. Duration weighting prevents irregular sub-window cadence from manufacturing coverage. Frozen-anchor provenance prevents a contaminated or outcome-selected member from quietly becoming the campaign&#39;s new recovery reference. The doctor remains useful as an early advisor without claiming more than its snapshot can prove.</p> <p>Consequences: campaign and bundle contracts gain policy/preflight/admission provenance, environment snapshots gain nullable display/screensaver/HID fields plus a post-run observation, and D-014&#39;s recovery wording is governed by cooldown v2 for new evidence. This decision is separate from AUD-WO-033, which remains behavior-preserving; D-077 intentionally changes future measurement admission and cooldown behavior and does not reinterpret sealed historical bundles.</p> <p>Revisit when: live quiet-window validation contradicts the defensive <code>pmset -g systemstate</code> display parser; calibrated platform data justifies an absolute ceiling; or a new platform cannot expose an equivalent critical probe without privilege.</p> <p>Fix-round amendment (2026-07-18): review found that summing sub-window durations as the completeness test made small inter-probe gaps reject an otherwise complete wall-clock window. Cooldown v2 now requires both a retained wall-clock span of at least <code>sustained_window_s</code> and captured coverage of at least <code>coverage_fraction * sustained_window_s</code>, with <code>coverage_fraction</code> defaulting to 0.8 and recorded in thresholds, trace rows, and release evidence. The same fix round made the existing frozen-reference rule operational for controller repetitions, attached cooldown evidence to each physical repetition (and each AXI entry), froze the first eligible repetition in execution order, re-probed the full governed environment per repetition, and added a guard observation after every idle capture. Environment-preflight early exits now retain a terminal campaign verdict; missing screensaver defaults domains use the macOS 20-minute default; and the two D-077 claim barriers are registered in the canonical reducer vocabulary. These are defect corrections to the accepted policy, not new policy alternatives.</p> <nav class="doc-meta" aria-label="Decision log parts"><span>Decision log parts:</span> <a href="decision_log.html">Recent</a> · <strong aria-current="page">Archive 1</strong></nav> </div> </div> </main> <footer class="site"> <div class="inner"> <span>JouleWise · github.com/mpmdw/JouleWise</span> <span>docs/decision_log.md · commit 1af9f92 + uncommitted · regenerate: <span class="mono">python3 scripts/build_site.py</span></span> </div> </footer> </body> </html>

class="source-file">docs/<wbr>contracts/<wbr>measurement_methodology.md</span><span class="source-commit">commit 6d80039</span></span></div> <!-- rendered: marked@18.0.6 --> <h1>Measurement Methodology</h1> <p>Living cross-phase contract, drafted in Phase 1. Changes require a decision-log entry when they bind later work.</p> <h2 id="measurement-principle">Measurement Principle</h2> <p>Every benchmark run must be reproducible from its raw artifacts. Summary metrics are derived outputs, not the source of truth.</p> <p>The source of truth for a run is the run bundle:</p> <ul> <li>Experiment config.</li> <li>Device and environment metadata.</li> <li>Event log with phase timestamps.</li> <li>Raw power trace.</li> <li>Raw model output.</li> <li>Reducer output.</li> <li>Runtime and telemetry logs.</li> </ul> <h2 id="run-lifecycle">Run Lifecycle</h2> <p>Before a campaign creates a run bundle, the operator runs the read-only doctor preflight described in <code>docs/contracts/doctor_preflight.md</code>. Schema-0.1 parsing continues to warn-and-ignore unknown keys for compatibility, but campaign execution fails before the first bundle when those warnings have not been explicitly acknowledged. The terminal campaign-verdict JSONL row records the exact warning set and acknowledgement; acknowledgement does not alter config bytes, collection evidence, claim readiness, or claim outcomes.</p> <p>Doctor also exposes architecture/version, configured model and tokenizer identity, requested sampler fields, inspect-only powermetrics privilege policy, thermal pressure, backup capacity, and quiet-machine warnings. These are preflight observations, not substitutes for per-bundle provenance or live measurement gates. In particular, doctor never starts powermetrics and never certifies that a machine is quiet.</p> <h3>Environment guard and per-run admission (D-077)</h3> <p>Campaigns select a strictly typed policy sidecar. <code>run_campaign.py</code> defaults to <code>configs/campaign_policies/quiet_mac_p2_production.json</code>, records the policy version and exact source-byte SHA-256 in campaign provenance and every member bundle, acquires the campaign lock, and only then performs the enforcing environment preflight before member 1. The production quiet-Mac guard requires AC power and an externally connected power source, low-power mode off, all online displays asleep, the screensaver disengaged, and Nominal thermal pressure. Unknown critical probes fail closed. Load averages are recorded as preflight evidence only and never gate a member.</p> <p>Default operation is verify-only. <code>--arm-quiet-mode</code> is an explicit transient operation: the runner displays a countdown, requests <code>pmset displaysleepnow</code>, and repeats the complete environment probe before deciding admission. It does not write display-sleep, screensaver, or other persistent host settings. An operator override is accepted only when its JSON binds the exact failed snapshot and findings SHA-256 values and records a reason, approver, and timestamp. It is stored as an <code>override</code>, not a waiver, and universally bars all resulting members from gross-energy, idle-subtracted-energy, and throughput claims.</p> <p>At each governed member&#39;s idle-baseline stage, the controller captures the same critical environment evidence and verifies that the display remains asleep and the screensaver remains disengaged. Awake, engaged, or unknown state aborts immediately. The first idle baseline is admitted only when the existing powermetrics GPU-idle-quality classification records <code>idle_window_suspect == false</code>. One and only one complete retry is allowed; both attempts preserve distinct raw artifacts and provenance. A persistent failure either aborts (production) or records the exploratory-only, unwaivable <code>environment_admission_failed</code> claim barrier (<code>on_fail: flag</code>). There is no skip disposition in a fixed-n campaign. A lightweight post-run display/screensaver/HID observation makes within-member transitions visible.</p> <p>The sidecar is deliberately separate from <code>BenchmarkConfig</code>. Direct <code>joulewise run</code> without a sidecar retains legacy flag-only/non-enforcing behavior, and omission of the additive policy/admission metadata preserves legacy normalized config serialization and hashes.</p> <h3>Per-bundle source provenance</h3> <p><code>RunBundleWriter.create</code> captures the harness source state before it creates bundle artifacts or returns control to any adapter. <code>write_metadata</code> captures the end state after adapter execution. <code>metadata.git_commit</code> remains the creation-time commit for compatibility; the governed record is <code>metadata.source_provenance</code> with schema <code>joulewise.source_provenance.v1</code>.</p> <p>Each <code>start</code> and <code>end</code> snapshot records <code>git_commit</code>, <code>tracked</code>, <code>staged</code>, <code>untracked</code>, and <code>diff_sha256</code>. The three state values are independently:</p> <ul> <li><code>clean</code>: the corresponding Git probe succeeded and found no change;</li> <li><code>dirty</code>: an unstaged tracked diff, staged diff, or non-ignored untracked path was present, respectively; or</li> <li><code>unknown</code>: the corresponding probe or required file read failed. Failure is never interpreted as clean.</li> </ul> <p>The privacy-safe diff identity descriptor is <code>sha256</code> / <code>joulewise.git-diff.nul-v1</code>. The producer captures the byte output of <code>git diff --no-ext-diff --no-textconv --binary</code>, the analogous <code>--cached</code> command, and <code>git ls-files --others --exclude-standard -z</code>. For each sorted untracked path it hashes, without serializing, the NUL-safe length-framed path, file kind, mode, size, and SHA-256 of regular-file bytes or symlink-target bytes. The final identity is SHA-256 over the version plus length-framed <code>tracked</code>, <code>staged</code>, and untracked-inventory byte identities. Bundles contain only the final digest and state labels: never a diff, path, untracked file content, or secret.</p> <p><code>changed_during_run</code> is true when two fully known snapshots differ, false when they match, and null when either snapshot is not fully known. <code>claim_eligible</code> is true only when both commits and diff identities are known, all six component states are clean, and the snapshots match. <code>reason_codes</code> is the deterministic list of every start/end unknown or dirty component followed, when applicable, by <code>source_changed_during_run</code>. Bundle completion remains allowed in every state so raw evidence is not discarded.</p> <p>Dirty, unknown, changed, missing, or internally inconsistent provenance is a hard exclusion for claim-bearing use. The publication pack preflight enforces that boundary and refuses such bundles. Analysis-side admission propagation is separate from capture and field semantics and is owned by WO-004/T11.</p> <ol> <li>Validate config.</li> <li>Create run directory.</li> <li>Collect device metadata.</li> <li>Measure idle baseline.</li> <li>Warm up runtime.</li> <li>Wait the configured post-warmup settling interval (<code>sampling.warmup_seconds</code>; zero means no wait).</li> <li>Start measured telemetry.</li> <li>Run workload.</li> <li>Stop measured telemetry.</li> <li>Cleanup runtime.</li> <li>Reduce raw artifacts into summary metrics.</li> </ol> <p>The post-warmup settling interval begins only after all active <code>workload_profile.warmup_runs</code> calls and their clock-alignment captures have completed. It ends before the measured-run stage and sampling-active markers, so it is never integrated into the measured window. Controller events record the configured value on the warmup completion event and the runtime log records positive waits.</p> <h2 id="idle-subtraction">Idle Subtraction</h2> <p>Energy metrics must report both gross and idle-subtracted values when possible. The idle baseline is measured before each run and stored in the run bundle.</p> <p>Minimum idle fields:</p> <ul> <li><code>idle_power_w_mean</code></li> <li><code>idle_power_w_stddev</code></li> <li><code>idle_duration_s</code></li> <li><code>idle_sample_count</code></li> <li><code>telemetry_backend</code></li> </ul> <h2 id="thermal-state">Thermal State</h2> <p>Each telemetry backend should report thermal state before and after measured runs when the platform exposes it.</p> <p>Minimum thermal fields:</p> <ul> <li><code>temperature_c</code></li> <li><code>thermal_pressure</code> or platform equivalent, when available.</li> <li><code>fan_state</code> or cooling mode, when available.</li> </ul> <h2 id="uncertainty">Uncertainty</h2> <p>Phase 1 defines uncertainty fields; Phase 2 implements reducer behavior. Repeated runs should report:</p> <ul> <li>Number of repetitions.</li> <li>Mean.</li> <li>Standard deviation.</li> <li>Confidence interval method.</li> <li>Confidence interval bounds.</li> </ul> <h2 id="measurement-quality-fields">Measurement Quality Fields</h2> <p>Each run summary should include:</p> <ul> <li>Sampling rate requested.</li> <li>Sampling rate observed.</li> <li>Dropped or malformed samples.</li> <li>Idle variance.</li> <li>Thermal drift.</li> <li>Telemetry source.</li> <li>Local runtime cleanup result (<code>runtime_cleanup_ok</code>: true/false/null). Cleanup occurs after the measured window, so failure is a quality concern for the following repetition and does not retroactively change current-run status or energy.</li> <li>Wall-meter comparison delta, when available.</li> </ul> <h2 id="phase-labels">Phase Labels</h2> <p>The event log should use stable phase names:</p> <ul> <li><code>idle</code></li> <li><code>warmup</code></li> <li><code>prefill</code></li> <li><code>decode</code></li> <li><code>serialize</code></li> <li><code>transfer</code></li> <li><code>deserialize</code></li> <li><code>cleanup</code></li> <li><code>failure</code></li> </ul> <p><code>deserialize</code> (cache load on the decode node) was added 2026-06-09 alongside the split-run accounting definitions (see <code>docs/phase_3/phase_3_plan.md</code>); phase labels are strings in the schema, so the addition is non-breaking. Split-stage accounting, pinned so reducers and prose agree: serialize = cache-persist window on the prefill node; transfer = byte-movement window; deserialize = cache-load window on the decode node; decode = first-token to last-token. Cache load is not decode energy.</p> <h2 id="hardware-classification">Hardware Classification</h2> <p>Every target should end Phase 1 in one state:</p> <ul> <li><code>supported</code>: known viable and ready for Phase 2 implementation.</li> <li><code>pending</code>: expected viable but not fully checked.</li> <li><code>unsupported</code>: not viable for a documented technical reason.</li> </ul> <h2 id="measurement-boundaries">Measurement Boundaries</h2> <p>&quot;Power&quot; means a different physical boundary on each telemetry backend. Cross-target absolute comparisons must state the boundary difference; the final report&#39;s limitations section inherits this table. Decision D-018 defines the rail policy (per-rail trace rows plus a per-backend rail manifest naming the canonical sum).</p> <div class="table-scroll"><table> <thead> <tr> <th>Backend</th> <th>Boundary</th> <th>Included</th> <th>Excluded</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody><tr> <td>powermetrics</td> <td>Apple SoC subsystems</td> <td>CPU + GPU + ANE package power</td> <td>display, storage, memory at wall, PSU losses</td> </tr> <tr> <td>nvidia_smi</td> <td>GPU board</td> <td>board power as reported by driver</td> <td>host CPU, DRAM, motherboard, PSU losses</td> </tr> <tr> <td>jetson_rails</td> <td>module input (VDD_IN preferred; actual rail recorded)</td> <td>module power</td> <td>carrier-board peripherals (rail-dependent), PSU losses</td> </tr> <tr> <td>wall_meter</td> <td>full system AC</td> <td>everything incl. PSU losses</td> <td>nothing</td> </tr> <tr> <td>mock</td> <td>synthetic</td> <td>n/a</td> <td>n/a</td> </tr> </tbody></table></div> <p>Rules:</p> <ul> <li>Within-target comparisons (the same backend) are always boundary-consistent and are the primary claim type.</li> <li>Cross-target comparisons are reported with boundaries named; where the wall meter exists, the wall-vs-platform delta is recorded per target and used to contextualize the gap.</li> <li>Each telemetry adapter declares its rail manifest in <code>device_metadata</code>; the reducer sums exactly the manifest rails to produce <code>power_w</code>.</li> </ul> <h2 id="clock-synchronization-and-multi-node-alignment">Clock Synchronization And Multi-Node Alignment</h2> <p>Policy per decision D-003:</p> <ul> <li>Canonical <code>timestamp_s</code> everywhere is epoch UTC from <code>time.time()</code> via the injected clock; no other time base appears in artifacts.</li> <li>Each process records its monotonic-vs-wall offset at start in metadata (detects wall-clock steps mid-run).</li> <li>Each node records NTP sync state in metadata when determinable.</li> <li>For multi-node runs, the controller bounds per-node clock offset with marker events: timestamp a no-op command on the remote node immediately before and after each remote stage; half the round trip bounds the offset. The bound is recorded in composite-bundle metadata.</li> <li>Reducers must flag (in measurement quality) any cross-node interval shorter than the recorded offset bound; such intervals are not used for energy attribution claims.</li> <li>Required precision: at 1-10 Hz power sampling, tens of milliseconds - comfortably within LAN NTP plus the marker bound.</li> </ul> <h2 id="controller-co-residency-controller-as-dut">Controller Co-Residency (Controller-As-DUT)</h2> <p>On Mac-local runs the controller process runs on the measured machine. Mitigation per decision D-013:</p> <ul> <li>The idle baseline is measured with the controller resident and quiescent, so the controller&#39;s floor load is included in what idle subtraction removes.</li> <li>During the measured window the controller only blocks on the runtime: no logging, no polling, no file writes; log records buffer in memory and flush after sampling stops.</li> <li>Residual risk is recorded, not hidden: OS background activity affects idle and measured windows alike; the upgrade path (remote-controlled Mac runs once the SSH transport exists) is queued as a validation comparison.</li> </ul> <h2 id="repetition-ordering-and-thermal-equilibrium">Repetition, Ordering, And Thermal Equilibrium</h2> <p>Per decisions D-005 and D-014:</p> <ul> <li>Each repetition is an independent run bundle; an experiment manifest groups members and records the executed order.</li> <li>Between live repetitions, cooldown v2 holds until the retained evidence has both a complete 30-second wall-clock span and at least <code>coverage_fraction * sustained_window_s</code> of captured coverage (<code>coverage_fraction = 0.8</code> by default), and its duration-weighted idle-power mean satisfies the one-sided rule <code>rolling_mean &lt;= reference * (1 + tolerance)</code> (10% by the production policy), while thermal pressure is Nominal. A below-reference mean therefore counts as recovery. An optional calibrated absolute ceiling is an additional upper cap and never an OR escape. The wait has a 5-minute cap; the cap is evaluated before release on every iteration, so recovery criteria first met at or after the deadline remain a <code>cap_hit</code> (with the late criteria recorded in the trace) and are recorded in the following repetition&#39;s measurement quality.</li> <li>The preceding baseline is eligible as a cooldown reference only when <code>idle_window_suspect == false</code>, all critical environment probes passed, and policy/environment provenance is present. An ineligible or unknown reference falls back to one frozen clean anchor: the NEG-8 reference start when present, otherwise the first admission-passing baseline. The anchor&#39;s source and hashes are recorded and it is never updated from later outcomes. With neither an eligible reference nor an anchor the gate fails closed. The following member records policy version, eligibility decision, anchor provenance, thresholds (including <code>coverage_fraction</code>), wall-clock span, required and observed coverage, thermal result, and the exact release criterion under <code>preceding_campaign_cooldown</code>. Historical recovered rows retain their recorded meaning and are not reinterpreted.</li> <li>Conditions are interleaved round-robin where model-reload cost permits; where blocks are operationally forced, the order is recorded so drift correlation can be audited (Phase 4 Stage 4.5 does this audit).</li> </ul> <h2 id="statistical-protocol">Statistical Protocol</h2> <p>Per decision D-014 (draft to be ratified against observed variance at Phase 4 Stage 4.0), amended 2026-07-09 (C-023 S3; amendments ratified by D-053):</p> <ul> <li>Repetitions: n &gt;= 5 for headline comparisons; n &gt;= 3 minimum elsewhere; the n is recorded per experiment.</li> <li>Intervals: report mean, sample standard deviation, and 95% confidence interval via Student t; Phase 4 runs a bootstrap sensitivity comparison and reports both where they materially disagree.</li> <li>Outliers: flagged by modified z-score on MAD &gt; 3.5; never silently dropped; reported with-and-without only when a physical cause is identified and documented; otherwise kept in headline numbers. Amendment 2026-07-09 (C-023 S3, ratified by D-053): at n &lt;= 10, reports also run a leave-one-out influence check on every claim-bearing contrast. The report lists the full-data estimate/CI/verdict and each leave-one-out estimate/CI/verdict. An omitted point is influential if it changes the sign, floor status, adjusted rejection/equivalence verdict, or moves the estimate by more than 0.25 x the active threshold: MDE for rank/MDE-gated claims, otherwise the floor gate. Influential points are reported as sensitivity evidence, not silently removed.</li> <li>Figures always show raw points alongside aggregates.</li> <li>Amendment 2026-07-09 (C-023 S3, ratified by D-053): differences are claimed from the confidence interval of the paired/block difference, or from the named model contrast, not by visual separation of marginal intervals. Where execution order was randomized, the analysis includes a permutation/randomization check for the same contrast following the actual randomization scheme, permuting labels only within exchangeable blocks/strata. The minimum for this check is 6 exchangeable blocks; below that count, report the check as not run and rely on the contrast CI with the caveat that randomization-inference sensitivity was underpowered. A paired contrast is preferred when it matches the design; mixed or hierarchical models are reserved for real dependence structures that a paired/block contrast cannot represent. Floor-gated outcomes use a three-way rule: below-floor contrasts are <code>not resolvable</code>; above-floor contrasts whose CI does not support direction are <code>unresolved</code> with no directional claim; equivalence or &quot;no difference&quot; language requires a predeclared equivalence gate whose margin exceeds the floor and whose contrast CI lies entirely within that margin.</li> </ul> </div> </div> </main> <footer class="site"> <div class="inner"> <span>JouleWise · github.com/mpmdw/JouleWise</span> <span>docs/contracts/measurement_methodology.md · commit 6d80039 · regenerate: <span class="mono">python3 scripts/build_site.py</span></span> </div> </footer> </body> </html>

6d80039</span></span></div> <!-- rendered: marked@18.0.6 --> <h1>Measurement Methodology</h1> <p>Living cross-phase contract, drafted in Phase 1. Changes require a decision-log entry when they bind later work.</p> <h2 id="measurement-principle">Measurement Principle</h2> <p>Every benchmark run must be reproducible from its raw artifacts. Summary metrics are derived outputs, not the source of truth.</p> <p>The source of truth for a run is the run bundle:</p> <ul> <li>Experiment config.</li> <li>Device and environment metadata.</li> <li>Event log with phase timestamps.</li> <li>Raw power trace.</li> <li>Raw model output.</li> <li>Reducer output.</li> <li>Runtime and telemetry logs.</li> </ul> <h2 id="run-lifecycle">Run Lifecycle</h2> <p>Before a campaign creates a run bundle, the operator runs the read-only doctor preflight described in <code>docs/contracts/doctor_preflight.md</code>. Schema-0.1 parsing continues to warn-and-ignore unknown keys for compatibility, but campaign execution fails before the first bundle when those warnings have not been explicitly acknowledged. The terminal campaign-verdict JSONL row records the exact warning set and acknowledgement; acknowledgement does not alter config bytes, collection evidence, claim readiness, or claim outcomes.</p> <p>Doctor also exposes architecture/version, configured model and tokenizer identity, requested sampler fields, inspect-only powermetrics privilege policy, thermal pressure, backup capacity, and quiet-machine warnings. These are preflight observations, not substitutes for per-bundle provenance or live measurement gates. In particular, doctor never starts powermetrics and never certifies that a machine is quiet.</p> <h3>Environment guard and per-run admission (D-077)</h3> <p>Campaigns select a strictly typed policy sidecar. <code>run_campaign.py</code> defaults to <code>configs/campaign_policies/quiet_mac_p2_production.json</code>, records the policy version and exact source-byte SHA-256 in campaign provenance and every member bundle, acquires the campaign lock, and only then performs the enforcing environment preflight before member 1. The production quiet-Mac guard requires AC power and an externally connected power source, low-power mode off, all online displays asleep, the screensaver disengaged, and Nominal thermal pressure. Unknown critical probes fail closed. Load averages are recorded as preflight evidence only and never gate a member.</p> <p>Default operation is verify-only. <code>--arm-quiet-mode</code> is an explicit transient operation: the runner displays a countdown, requests <code>pmset displaysleepnow</code>, and repeats the complete environment probe before deciding admission. It does not write display-sleep, screensaver, or other persistent host settings. An operator override is accepted only when its JSON binds the exact failed snapshot and findings SHA-256 values and records a reason, approver, and timestamp. It is stored as an <code>override</code>, not a waiver, and universally bars all resulting members from gross-energy, idle-subtracted-energy, and throughput claims.</p> <p>At each governed member&#39;s idle-baseline stage, the controller captures the same critical environment evidence and verifies that the display remains asleep and the screensaver remains disengaged. Awake, engaged, or unknown state aborts immediately. The first idle baseline is admitted only when the existing powermetrics GPU-idle-quality classification records <code>idle_window_suspect == false</code>. One and only one complete retry is allowed; both attempts preserve distinct raw artifacts and provenance. A persistent failure either aborts (production) or records the exploratory-only, unwaivable <code>environment_admission_failed</code> claim barrier (<code>on_fail: flag</code>). There is no skip disposition in a fixed-n campaign. Direct <code>joulewise run</code> without a sidecar retains legacy flag-only/non-enforcing behavior, and omission of the additive policy/admission metadata preserves legacy normalized config serialization and hashes.</p> <h3>Per-bundle source provenance</h3> <p><code>RunBundleWriter.create</code> captures the harness source state before it creates bundle artifacts or returns control to any adapter. <code>write_metadata</code> captures the end state after adapter execution. <code>metadata.git_commit</code> remains the creation-time commit for compatibility; the governed record is <code>metadata.source_provenance</code> with schema <code>joulewise.source_provenance.v1</code>.</p> <p>Each <code>start</code> and <code>end</code> snapshot records <code>git_commit</code>, <code>tracked</code>, <code>staged</code>, <code>untracked</code>, and <code>diff_sha256</code>. Failure is never interpreted as clean.</li> </ul> <p>The privacy-safe diff identity descriptor is <code>sha256</code> / <code>joulewise.git-diff.nul-v1</code>. The producer captures the byte output of <code>git diff --no-ext-diff --no-textconv --binary</code>, the analogous <code>--cached</code> command, and <code>git ls-files --others --exclude-standard -z</code>. For each sorted untracked path it hashes, without serializing, the NUL-safe length-framed path, file kind, mode, size, and SHA-256 of regular-file bytes or symlink-target bytes. The final identity is SHA-256 over the version plus length-framed <code>tracked</code>, <code>staged</code>, and untracked-inventory byte identities. Bundles contain only the final digest and state labels: never a diff, path, untracked file content, or secret.</p> <p><code>changed_during_run</code> is true when two fully known snapshots differ, false when they match, and null when either snapshot is not fully known. <code>claim_eligible</code> is true only when both commits and diff identities are known, all six component states are clean, and the snapshots match. <code>reason_codes</code> is the deterministic list of every start/end unknown or dirty component followed, when applicable, by <code>source_changed_during_run</code>.
